102a7353-3de7-46ba-822d-43ff0b4d8491.description: This major prepares you to become a civil engineer by combining contemporary theory with industry-led projects. You'll build the skills to confidently design, construct and maintain the built infrastructure systems that are essential to everyday life. Learn to apply scientific and engineering principles to solve complex problems and develop innovative solutions that benefit both organisations and the wider community. Throughout the major, you'll explore a diverse range of civil engineering disciplines, including structural, water, geotechnical and transportation engineering, as well as civil engineering materials. This major is studied within Deakin's Bachelor of Engineering (Honours), which prepares you for professional engineering practice through project-based learning, industry connections and 60 days of professional placement.

85bdb3dc-f00e-49a6-a8d0-077f4581c004._name: Bachelor of Communication and Creative Arts (Honours)
85bdb3dc-f00e-49a6-a8d0-077f4581c004.description: Explore advanced creative projects and research through a Bachelor of Communication and Creative Arts (Honours). Undertake specialised study combining the theory and practical skills gained throughout your undergraduate degree. With a strong interdisciplinary focus, you will collaborate with students from across communication and creative arts disciplines, including dance, theatre, film, television, animation, photography, design, digital media and visual arts, while developing your creative practice and scholarly research skills. Guided and supported by a supervisor you will undertake an individual creative project. You will build your skills, critical engagement and depth of knowledge in your chosen area of study. Look forward to expanding your knowledge in an area you are passionate about and gaining invaluable research and life skills. On graduation you can continue studying into the Master of Fine Arts or a Master of Arts, or you could pursue a PhD.

8692f3c5-f3eb-4535-9270-0fec033c07c2.description: Deakin's Bachelor of Construction Management (Honours) equips you with market-ready skills for construction management, quantity surveying and property development. You will develop an in-depth understanding of the business of construction, including economics, finance, law, technology, and sustainability. With a strong focus on practical learning, you will develop the initiative to work confidently from day one across projects large and small. Industry placements, site visits and studio-based work help you gain professional experience while building professional networks, technical knowledge and skills. You will also collaborate with Deakin's architecture students to gain a sound understanding across both disciplines. This experience prepares you for the real world and ensures you graduate with the well-rounded and adaptable skill set employers are looking for.

7ef2d65c-2e1c-4f14-b6d6-d4386128f6ac._name: Bachelor of Electrical and Electronics Engineering (Honours)
7ef2d65c-2e1c-4f14-b6d6-d4386128f6ac.description: This major (offered by Deakin today as Electrical and Renewable Energy Engineering) prepares you with the skills and experience required to confidently tackle modern engineering challenges, with a particular emphasis on electrical and renewable energy design and communication technologies. Whether you study on campus or online, you will have access to the latest electrical engineering tools and application software, from renewable energy, power systems and high-voltage (HV) labs, to Deakin's microgrid facility with battery storage and a Research, Teaching and Visualisation Centre. This major is studied within Deakin's Bachelor of Engineering (Honours).

ef30b32a-e5c5-4488-8ec8-e9cb3416c2af.description: This course allows you to deepen your understanding of a chosen environmental science discipline, while building key research and transferable skills that enhance your employment options and prepare you for further study. Honours is an optional year of specialised study that allows you to build on the theory and practical skills gained throughout your undergraduate studies. It is an opportunity to showcase your expertise in a discipline you are passionate about, while developing invaluable research and life skills that will stay with you throughout your entire career.

ce86bb7c-b063-4055-a03a-2a98145805b1._name: Bachelor of Health and Medical Science (Honours)
ce86bb7c-b063-4055-a03a-2a98145805b1.description: Gain a competitive edge in your career and make a meaningful contribution to health or medical science research. The Bachelor of Health and Medical Science (Honours) gives you the opportunity to build on your undergraduate studies through an additional year of advanced coursework, research training and independent investigation. You'll deepen your knowledge in your chosen health or medical science discipline while developing the critical thinking, investigative and research skills needed to tackle real-world challenges. As well as studying research methodology, you'll complete an independent research project under the supervision of experienced researchers with expertise across health and medicine. Graduate with the skills and experience to pursue opportunities in academia, government, private industry, biological sciences, clinical research and beyond. You'll also be well prepared for further study, including higher degrees by research.

cc9639b9-4d25-4790-9c6d-36b75618e7e7.description: Understand the human mind in the business context and apply psychological science to the real workplace challenges faced in human resource management. Develop dual expertise to make confident, evidence-based decisions in recruitment, workplace negotiations and creating high-performance work environments and gain a competitive edge for a human resources career. Build targeted knowledge in psychology and human resources and develop practical skills that employers value. Your strong understanding of human behaviour will help you assess employee performance, support positive organisational culture and select the right person for each role. The course is aligned with key accreditation bodies, including the Australian HR Institute (AHRI) and the Australian Psychology Accreditation Council (APAC), and closely reflects industry needs, with practical learning experiences such as industry placements and opportunities for overseas study.

e88be117-422c-41be-b458-1cc43dcc639c.description: Understand what truly motivates consumers by combining marketing and psychology to deeply analyse consumer behaviour and turn insights into powerful marketing campaigns that deliver real results. Develop practical skills in marketing strategy, consumer behaviour, digital marketing and data driven decision-making, while building a deep understanding of how people think, feel and act. With its industry focus, practical projects and 80+ hours of work-integrated learning, the Bachelor of Marketing (Psychology) will help you turn theory into experience that stands out to employers. You will graduate prepared for roles in brand management, market research, customer experience and digital marketing and progress to becoming a Certified Practising Marketer. Or choose to continue your studies towards becoming a registered psychologist.

179b6d7e-23dd-49a2-81e8-662cb929a05b.description: Mechanical engineers are crucial to the design and development of the complex systems, devices and machinery needed to tackle future global challenges. These include health assistive technologies and biomedical devices, renewable energy systems, advanced manufacturing facilities and low emissions transport. You will combine contemporary theory with industry-led projects to hone the skills required to develop and operate the innovative mechanical systems and technologies of tomorrow. This major is studied within Deakin's Bachelor of Engineering (Honours).

b8ec1dc4-c2f2-4f85-bfec-f07772233d73.description: This major prepares you to be a practical and industry-ready engineer capable of designing the electronics, robots and autonomous systems of the future. You will learn how to design, program and integrate electronic devices with mechanical designs that communicate with other computers, devices or even cloud-based systems. You will be able to deliver innovative solutions to real-world problems and design autonomous and intelligent devices ranging from self-driving vehicles to biomedical systems. This major is studied within Deakin's Bachelor of Engineering (Honours).

83384917-a230-48ff-ad72-fb966d3fd597.description: Create the smart software and systems of the future by studying Deakin's Bachelor of Software Engineering (Honours). This course arms you with the skills needed to build disruptive technologies that create change, making you a sought-after expert ready to solve tomorrow's business problems through creative computing solutions. Explore a broad range of exciting study areas, including robotics, algorithms, programming and software architecture, and apply your skills in world-class facilities. Gain practical experience and learn to work successfully in teams through project-based learning. Contribute to industry projects alongside professional engineers during placements. You will build specialised skills in robotics, cyber-physical systems and the Internet-of-Things (IoT), while using the latest software engineering tools to develop advanced, intelligent and real-world solutions beyond traditional technologies.

17297069-ecb7-47ee-a627-b7bebc2b4774.description: Study medicine in a program designed to improve the health and wellbeing of the communities we serve, by focussing on excellence, innovation and developing work readiness in our graduates. Deakin's Doctor of Medicine has a distinctive focus on rural and regional medicine, Indigenous health, patient-centred care and service to marginalised communities, preparing you to make a meaningful difference through your future medical career. From your first year, you will engage with a full-time study load to develop foundational knowledge in medical sciences, clinical practice, public health, ethics and Indigenous health while building the communication, clinical reasoning and professional skills essential for contemporary medical practice. In Years 1 and 2, through problem-based learning, interactive sessions and immersive hands-on laboratory and clinical experiences, you will learn to apply your knowledge on campus and in real healthcare settings and develop confidence working with patients, families and multidisciplinary healthcare teams. In Years 3 and 4, students experience full-time clinical placements across hospitals, general practices and community health settings that provide opportunities to experience medicine across diverse populations and environments. In your final years, you will undertake full-time clinical training through one of Deakin's medical school sites across Victoria, gaining hands-on experience that prepares you for professional practice, lifelong learning and a wide range of medical career pathways.

4e3ee0b0-5a0c-4487-a528-d2ed3fafc7e9.description: Study Deakin's Graduate Certificate of Fine Arts to build on your undergraduate skills and explore contemporary approaches to creativity. Refine your practice through practical learning and collaboration while developing transferable skills such as imaginative thinking, problem solving and leadership. Learn, create and experiment alongside thinkers from a range of backgrounds in a supportive environment. Complete electives that let you deepen your strengths or build capability in a new area. Through industry-relevant projects and practice in professional-standard creative facilities, you will apply ideas in individual and team settings. Strengthen your practice while becoming a more reflective and adaptable creative professional. On graduation, choose from a range of creative career opportunities or continue your studies by articulating into Deakin's Master of Fine Arts.

1298e690-4a8d-4dd5-9b31-a5ccbf7fe4df._name: Graduate Certificate of Health and Medical Research
1298e690-4a8d-4dd5-9b31-a5ccbf7fe4df.description: Help improve the lives of individuals and communities by learning to create evidence-based solutions that impact outcomes across Australia and around the globe with Deakin's Graduate Certificate of Health and Medical Research. Under the guidance of leading researchers, you will build skills in critical thinking, complex problem solving and communication. Working in world-class facilities, you will gain technical skills in research training, ethics and experiential research to demonstrate discipline specific knowledge and capabilities. You will graduate with skills highly sought after within academia, research institutes, hospitals, medical bodies and government health and science agencies. Graduate with the minimum requirements for PhD entry at Deakin University, and gain valuable experiential training around project planning, execution, presentation and thesis writing.

1a5f085c-f4ff-4e22-95b5-deb3b9a898f6.description: Challenge your imagination and take your creative practice further with Deakin's Graduate Diploma of Fine Arts. Explore the ideas shaping your field while building the critical, practical and collaborative skills employers value. Through projects and creative production, you will develop a portfolio that reflects your interests and professional goals. Learn in industry-grade facilities, including TV broadcast studios, dance and drama studios, a professional photographic light studio, visual arts and design studios and dedicated gallery spaces. Deepen your skillset by choosing from a wide range of electives, including writing with the camera, arts marketing, digital art and photography. Take part in internships, volunteering or on-campus practical experiences through studio work. By graduation, you will be ready to work as an adaptable, resourceful creative. You may also choose to continue building your creative expertise and articulate into Deakin's Master of Fine Arts.

230d9f78-ac60-473d-afc7-4c1038931758.description: Build on your undergraduate psychology studies and take the next step towards becoming a registered psychologist with the APAC-accredited Graduate Diploma of Psychology (Advanced). Designed for students seeking a recognised fourth-year psychology qualification, this course deepens your understanding of human behaviour while developing advanced skills in psychological assessment, counselling and research. Learn from experienced academics, explore contemporary areas of psychology and gain the analytical skills needed to formulate psychological opinions in professional practice. Accredited by the Australian Psychology Accreditation Council (APAC), the course allows eligible graduates to apply for provisional registration with the Psychology Board of Australia (PsyBA). It also provides a pathway to further APAC-accredited postgraduate study required for general registration as a psychologist. Study on campus or online and graduate with sought-after skills that can support careers across mental health, community services, public health and case management.

476b7dc8-6792-48b5-8861-61c49e04ad9d._name: Master of Artificial Intelligence for Design and Creative Practice
476b7dc8-6792-48b5-8861-61c49e04ad9d.description: Develop the skills to understand, evaluate and apply generative artificial intelligence (AI) in creative professional contexts with Deakin's two-year Master of Artificial Intelligence for Design and Creative Practice, Australia's first dedicated master's degree in AI for design and creative practice. Designed for ambitious creatives looking to responsibly integrate and enhance AI into creative workflows, the course helps you explore how AI is developed, how it can support and challenge creative work, and the ethical, social and professional responsibilities that come with its use. Learn through collaborative studio practice and in ethical labs, guided by industry-informed briefs. Test ideas, prototype responsibly and combine AI capability with human creative judgement. Tailor your study through electives, optional work-integrated learning and a research capstone, graduating ready to contribute across design, media and other creative practice settings.

9ec4bd60-4e64-4912-a3c2-f44a4e6759b2.description: Become an in-demand expert and create innovative solutions to global challenges with a Master of Biotechnology (Professional) at Deakin, from pioneering medical advancements to cutting-edge solutions for food, agricultural and environmental issues, gaining advanced technical skills to build a global career effecting positive change. Undertake up to 500 hours of placements with organisations specialising in food innovation, agricultural biotechnology, disease monitoring and analytical testing, such as Symbio Laboratories, Agromillora, CSIRO and Australian Clinical Labs. Learn under globally recognised researchers and discover how to apply your specialist knowledge across genetic, chemical, industrial and agricultural settings. Your biotechnology expertise will be complemented by skills in statistical data analysis, coding and research alongside a well-developed understanding of the commercial biotechnology environment.

35225b74-2c8c-4549-9337-fbdc3e2a8ad1.description: Deepen your expertise in a chosen area within the field of construction management through independent, sustained and academically supervised research. The Master of Construction Management (Research) gives you the opportunity to conduct research in the construction management and building disciplines. You will write a thesis explaining the research carried out in your field of study. To qualify for a Master by Research, you must demonstrate an advanced and integrated understanding of your research topic, completed in the form of a thesis of up to 50,000 words in length. Although the focus of the degree is on research, you will also be required to complete a minimum of one unit of coursework. When applying, contact the School of Architecture and Built Environment for guidance on developing research proposals.

bfd18cd7-747b-4873-800c-14abe5d8e8d9.description: Realise your full potential as a creator with Deakin's Master of Fine Arts. Built around studio practice, creative research and a major final project, this course helps you refine your creative voice and graduate with a standout portfolio. Be supported by discipline experts in areas such as dance, theatre, new media, photography, visual arts or visual communication design. Build transferable skills valued across the creative industries, including imaginative thinking, problem solving, collaboration, adaptability and research capability. The multidisciplinary aspect of the course means you might study dance, choose an elective in film writing and combine them for your final project and create a dance film. Through industry-relevant projects, internship opportunities and access to professional facilities, you will gain practical experience to shape your creative career or pursue higher degree by research.

7b498a56-a470-4e2e-a2ca-08df01196527.description: This is a supervised research program. The research of each candidate is conducted under the supervision of a full-time member of the academic staff. Candidates are required to participate in an oral colloquium about one third of the way through candidature in which the proposed research is defended, and will ultimately submit a thesis embodying the results of their research. The thesis may be a single volume of disciplinary scholarship or a folio consisting of an exegesis and two to four research products relating to professional practice. Candidates showing significant promise as research students may be invited to transfer their enrolment to the Doctor of Philosophy program. This generally occurs at or post colloquium. Transfer is dependent on meeting the academic requirements for PhD entry and must have the full support of the principal supervisor.

627442ca-bff4-4e10-9907-2a43baec3ada.description: Strong technical expertise alone is not enough in today's engineering industry, communication, project management and business strategy are just as critical. Take the next step in your engineering career with Deakin's Master of Engineering Management (Professional), a degree designed to build the leadership and management skills needed to succeed. Develop an awareness of engineering practice through continuing professional development opportunities aimed at providing contextual experience of the Australian Engineering Sector. Develop your engineering expertise while building the capability to lead teams and manage complex projects. You will refine your technical skills in a chosen engineering discipline while strengthening your knowledge of project management, communication and leadership. As a graduate, you will be primed to take on greater responsibility in engineering environments.

ddbe3bfe-3fea-4ad5-a1e1-99924d3e2e95.description: Study the Master of Humanitarianism and Development to develop a deeper understanding of the challenges facing the planet. Extend your theoretical knowledge and enhance your specialist and practical skills in international development, crisis and disaster response, humanitarian responses, and community development. You'll gain insights into the histories, causes, interconnections, and multiple impacts of the many crises facing the world. You'll also learn about community-led approaches to these issues that are occurring locally and across the globe. By identifying the challenges and successes of these strategies you'll understand how communities create new and far-reaching methods and processes for addressing social, political and environmental problems. Deakin has an exceptional reputation with over 40 years of teaching and research in international and community development, and more than a decade in humanitarian assistance, and was the first graduate program in humanitarian assistance in Australia. The Master of Humanitarianism and Development is designed with industry consultation and taught by pioneering academics.

987e7d9d-1157-4ae3-869b-4e360c853a88.description: This elite intensive research degree in health and (bio-) medical sciences will provide students with the opportunity to pursue an independent investigative research project under the supervision of an academic staff member in the School of Medicine, along with coursework specifically designed to provide relevant skills in research design, communication, integrity and interpretation. This course will provide students with a dedicated pathway into PhD programs or into employment where deeper disciplinary knowledge and research skills are required. The research projects that centre on the basis of health and disease span from basic gene discovery and molecular analysis, through to functional genomics and pre-clinical development, to clinical and population studies. This includes the fields of immunity, infectious diseases, developmental biology, exercise physiology and metabolism, musculoskeletal biology, haematology, cancer, metabolic disease, neuroscience, molecular psychiatry and nanomedicine. Research projects may also be offered in the field of rural and regional medicine, general practice, chronic disease management, public health, medical education, epidemiology, farmer health, medical imaging, surgery and optometry.

c0aeacc4-0050-4c51-aa88-004c7e801e30.description: Build advanced skills to support people experiencing mental health challenges through evidence-based psychological practice. The Master of Psychology (Clinical) prepares you for professional practice as a registered psychologist through advanced clinical training, research and placement experience. Accredited by the Australian Psychology Accreditation Council (APAC), the course provides the qualifications required to apply for general registration with the Psychology Board of Australia (PsyBA). This course also provides a pathway into the clinical registrar program to gain an area of practice endorsement with the PsyBA. You will develop capabilities in clinical assessment, diagnosis, and psychological intervention of mental health conditions, grounded in ethical, culturally responsive, and evidence-based practice. Clinical placements provide opportunities to apply your skills with clients under supervision. Through key partnerships across public and primary mental health settings, including Barwon Health, you will build professional experience and clinical confidence that support future endorsement pathways.

e5f2c1ee-2859-4d4b-b176-eeadce32b938.description: The Master of Research (Business) is a two-year degree designed to develop your research capabilities, immerse you in a major research project, and expose you to the latest thinking in your chosen discipline. This course offers a pathway to a research-focused career in industry and serves as a gateway to the PhD in Business and Law for those who want to pursue an academic career. In the first year of your Master of Research (Business) you will complete research training coursework units, covering the research thought process, research methods and the current state of theory in your chosen discipline. The second year is devoted to a major research project on a question of interest to you (subject to supervisory team approval) and includes your Research Proposal and Research Dissertation/Thesis.

4f331cb9-3fc4-4ac9-86bf-5111a145eaf5.description: If you are a qualified social worker, undertake further research training to develop expertise relevant to your practice. A Master of Social Work (Research) degree is awarded for a substantial, original contribution to knowledge achieved in up to two years of full-time study (or two to four years of part-time candidature). Research areas include social work theory and practice, critical social work, evidence bases in social work, social work education, human services provision, child and family welfare, mental health, diversity and inclusivity, religion and spirituality, masculinities, gender relations and gender violence.

ee53ab3c-c3a9-4348-9c71-edbbb7bb4f01.description: Learn to work in partnership with people experiencing communication or swallowing needs, and their carers, families and communities, to support participation, wellbeing and quality of life. With Deakin's Master of Speech Pathology, you will develop the knowledge, skills and practice-based experience to work confidently with people across the lifespan. Co-designed with people with disability, carers and advocates, the course has a unique focus on disability-informed practice, helping you develop specialised skills that set you apart in the workforce. You will build capability in communication and swallowing assessment and intervention, including working with people with disability, including complex disability, in person-centred, culturally responsive and collaborative ways. Practical experience is embedded throughout the course through active, creative and social learning, including interprofessional experiences and scaffolded placements and simulation-based learning.

9618176a-2046-4d47-93d4-1b700db400c2.description: This course of study leads to a Masters by Research degree, with students drawn from qualified medical practitioners, surgeons in training and fellowship-trained surgeons. The program has a primary function in providing doctors with a structured training and experience in independent research, specifically in the surgical speciality. It also fulfils a secondary function in providing discipline-specific training for doctors with aspirations in surgery, and provides an option for students to gain some skills in clinical leadership, for future leadership roles in surgery and broader medicine. Research training and clinical leadership training is carried out at the Waurn Ponds campus, with heavy utilisation of online resources to support the teaching. Research activity, although coordinated from the Waurn Ponds campus, will mainly be carried out at the student's place of work, although the School of Medicine's Anatomy Laboratory will also be utilised where the Clinical Anatomy Investigation project involves cadaveric inspection or dissection. Primary supervision is shared by academics within the School and other experts local to the workplace.

3f524e12-6a97-497d-a008-fd4c31685d9c.description: Study a Master of Teaching (Early Childhood) and learn how to help young children develop key skills like empathy and self-confidence through play. With 60+ days professional placement built-in, you will graduate prepared to shape the next generation. The course also combines online and on-campus learning, giving you the flexibility to balance work and study. Ranked #3 in Australia and #13 worldwide for education and educational research, Deakin is also the only university to embed the Berry Street Education Model, using trauma-informed strategies in all initial teaching degrees. You can choose to specialise in early childhood inquiry, trauma responsive practice or research pathways. You may also be able to fast track this two-year masters degree, graduating sooner and ready to manage safe, healthy and engaging learning environments that promote academic success. This course is approved by ACECQA as an early childhood teaching qualification in Australia.

1461aab9-7dc7-4fb9-934b-8af011274714.description: Deakin's Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) is a supervised research degree in which you make a substantial, original contribution to knowledge in your chosen field. You will work closely with a principal supervisor and one or more associate supervisors, expert academic staff who guide your research journey, while completing required research training coursework units. Deakin currently has around 1,600 higher degree by research candidates, supported by strong facilities, partnerships and strategic research centres. You will write a thesis of 80,000 to 100,000 words embodying the results of your research (creative arts candidates may instead submit a creative work with an accompanying exegesis of 25,000 to 50,000 words). The PhD is normally completed over three to four years of full-time study, or the part-time equivalent, and is offered across every faculty at Deakin, from Arts and Education to Business and Law, Science, Engineering and Built Environment, and Health.
1461aab9-7dc7-4fb9-934b-8af011274714.curriculum: The Doctor of Philosophy is a research-only higher degree with no set unit table. Candidates are appointed a principal supervisor and one or more associate supervisors and complete a compulsory 0-credit-point Academic Integrity and Respect at Deakin module (DAI001), plus any required research training coursework units, before undertaking a supervised research project. The degree is examined through a thesis of 80,000 to 100,000 words (or, for creative arts candidates, a creative work with a 25,000 to 50,000 word exegesis) embodying an original contribution to knowledge in the candidate's chosen field, normally completed over three to four years of full-time study or the part-time equivalent.
1461aab9-7dc7-4fb9-934b-8af011274714.admission_requirements: To be considered for selection into a Higher Degree by Research such as the PhD, you are required to have completed either a research project (including a thesis) equivalent to at least 25% of a year's full-time study at Level 8 or 9 of the Australian Qualifications Framework, with a grade equivalent to a Deakin grade of 70% or higher, or a masters degree (research) in a related area. Academic history, work and life experience, and individual circumstances are also considered.
1461aab9-7dc7-4fb9-934b-8af011274714.english_requirements: Bachelor degree from a recognised English-speaking country, or IELTS overall score of 7.0 (with no band score less than 6.5) or equivalent, or other evidence of English language proficiency.

386357ca-1c32-4df1-9ea8-89c85fab454e.description: Deakin's Master of Applied Science is a research masters degree available with a health focus, letting you undertake independent research under the supervision of an academic staff member across areas including Exercise and Sports Science, Food and Nutrition Sciences, Health and Medicine, Nursing and Midwifery, Occupational Science and Therapy, Clinical and Forensic Psychology, Public Health and Health Promotion, Health Economics and Program Evaluation, and Social Work. A Masters by Research degree is awarded for a substantial, original contribution to knowledge achieved in up to two years of full-time study (or two to four years of part-time candidature). Deakin currently has around 1,600 higher degree by research candidates, supported by excellent facilities, partnerships and strategic research centres. This degree is a strong foundation for a future career in research and academia.
386357ca-1c32-4df1-9ea8-89c85fab454e.curriculum: The Master of Applied Science is a research-only degree with no set unit table. You are appointed a principal supervisor from Deakin's academic staff and, under their supervision, undertake an independent research project in your chosen health-related area, completing a thesis of substantial original work. The degree is normally completed in up to two years of full-time study, or two to four years part-time.
386357ca-1c32-4df1-9ea8-89c85fab454e.admission_requirements: To be considered for selection into this degree you are required to have completed a research project including a thesis which is equivalent to at least 25% of a year's full-time study at Level 8 of the Australian Qualifications Framework, with achievement of a grade for the project equivalent to a Deakin grade of 65% or higher.
386357ca-1c32-4df1-9ea8-89c85fab454e.english_requirements: Bachelor degree from a recognised English-speaking country, or IELTS overall score of 7.0 (with no band score less than 6.5) or equivalent, or other evidence of English language proficiency.

79c640cd-c56d-4995-a642-14ce1586df7c._name: Master of Health and Human Services Management
79c640cd-c56d-4995-a642-14ce1586df7c.description: Deakin's Master of Health and Human Services Management prepares you for a career in the health and human services sector by developing skills in leadership, planning and service management. You will learn how to manage people, resources and programs while contributing to better outcomes for individuals and communities, applying business and management principles with a patient and community-focused approach to service delivery. You can tailor your degree through a choice of specialisations, including public health, health economics, business administration, disability and inclusion, sustainability in healthcare and research. With flexible online and on-campus study options, and opportunities for work-integrated learning or international study, you will graduate with the skills to work across a range of roles in the health and human services sector. This course is accredited by the Australasian College of Health Service Management, supporting your professional recognition and career progression.
79c640cd-c56d-4995-a642-14ce1586df7c.curriculum: All students complete core units, including a compulsory 0-credit-point Academic Integrity and Respect at Deakin module (DAI001), Fundamentals of Digital Health (HME704), Health Law and Ethics (HME711), Healthcare Operations (HME712), Principles and Practice of Public Health (HSH701) and Health Economics 1 (HSH717), before completing units in a chosen specialisation such as public health, health economics, business administration, disability and inclusion, sustainability in healthcare or research.
79c640cd-c56d-4995-a642-14ce1586df7c.admission_requirements: To be considered for admission to the 1.5-year pathway (with admission credit applied) you will need completion of a bachelor's degree or equivalent in a related discipline (such as nursing or allied health) plus at least two years of full-time equivalent relevant work experience (for example as a health professional, allied health science professional, medical administrator or health information manager). Without admission credit, the course is completed over 2 years full-time and requires only completion of a bachelor's degree in any discipline. Recognition of prior learning is considered on a case-by-case basis.
79c640cd-c56d-4995-a642-14ce1586df7c.english_requirements: Bachelor degree from a recognised English-speaking country, or IELTS overall score of 6.5 (with no band score less than 6.0) in each component of the test, or other evidence of English language proficiency.

96223e14-0806-4c76-a7aa-e683923f460e._name: Bachelor of Cyber Security (fabrication fix, curriculum only, found during spot-check)
96223e14-0806-4c76-a7aa-e683923f460e.curriculum: Year 1 - Trimester 1: Academic Integrity and Respect at Deakin (0 credit points, DAI001); Career Tools for Employability (0 credit points, STP010); Introduction to Programming (SIT102); Computer Systems (SIT111); Real World Practices for Cyber Security (SIT182); Discrete Mathematics (SIT192). Year 1 - Trimester 2: Computer Networks and Communication (SIT202); Object-Oriented Development (SIT232); plus 2 minor or open elective units. Year 2 - Trimester 1: Computer Forensics and Investigations (SIT282); Cyber Security Analytics (SIT384); plus 2 minor or open elective units. Year 2 - Trimester 2: Secure Coding (SIT218); Professional Practice in Information Technology (SIT223); plus 2 minor or open elective units. Year 3 - Trimester 1: Malware Analysis (SIT324); Network Forensics (SIT327); Team Project (A), Project Management and Practices (capstone, SIT374); plus 1 minor or open elective unit. Year 3 - Trimester 2: Ethical Hacking (SIT379); plus 1 minor or open elective unit; plus a capstone choice of Team Project (B), Execution and Delivery (SIT378) or IT Placements and Industry Experience (SIT306).

f8de3eac-96d9-4008-8315-3fb8e9d74722._name: Master of Business Administration (fabrication fix, curriculum only, found during spot-check)

ae9f4d8e-7339-4fec-8ada-f74e736e1820.description: Deakin's Master of Science is a research masters degree offered across specialisations in Biology and Chemical Sciences, Environmental Science, and Information Technology. Under the guidance of internationally recognised research staff, you undertake independent, sustained and academically supervised research to develop an advanced and integrated understanding of a complex body of knowledge in your chosen discipline area. You generate a substantial contribution to knowledge in your chosen area in the form of a thesis of up to 50,000 words, becoming an expert in your field and advancing your career prospects. Although the focus of the degree is on research, you will also complete at least one unit of coursework.
ae9f4d8e-7339-4fec-8ada-f74e736e1820.curriculum: The Master of Science is a research-only degree with no set unit table. Alongside at least one unit of coursework, you undertake an independent research project supervised by Deakin academic staff in your chosen specialisation (Biology and Chemical Sciences, Environmental Science, or Information Technology), producing a thesis of up to 50,000 words. The degree is normally completed in up to two years of full-time study, or the part-time equivalent.
ae9f4d8e-7339-4fec-8ada-f74e736e1820.admission_requirements: To be considered for selection into this degree you are required to have completed a research project including a thesis which is equivalent to at least 25% of a year's full-time study at Level 8 of the Australian Qualifications Framework, with achievement of a grade for the project equivalent to a Deakin grade of 65% or higher.
ae9f4d8e-7339-4fec-8ada-f74e736e1820.english_requirements: Bachelor degree from a recognised English-speaking country, or IELTS overall score of 6.5 (with no band score less than 6.0) in each component of the test, or other evidence of English language proficiency.
